OpenStreetMap and the Garmin nüvi GPS navigator, redux
Posted by apm-wa on 12 October 2026 in English.
1 have uploaded updates to Github of my personal scripts and style sheets for making Garmin-compatible IMG files out of OSM-origin PBF files
(thank you, Geofabrik!), both for Central Asia (all five countries) and for the Russian Federation.
The Russian Federation style sheets render names of highways and POls in both English and Russian to ease searching on a GPS unit,
wherever a name:en variable is available. Both sets of style sheets render foreign diplomatic missions as well as various other POls that for
whatever reason other providers of IMG files omit.
I found that generating individual IMG files, each with its own family-id=* number in the mkgmap script, then merging them into a single file
using GMapTool, allows the Garmin nüvi tolisteach map individually in MyMaps,which means they can be selected and deselected
individually. Since the gmapsupp.img files can be quite large and thus slow to load (and for the nüvi processor to process, especially for older
models) this is very handy. The Russia map is well over 2 gigabytes, and the Central Asia map is about 370 megabytes.
My Wintel desktop has 32Gb of RAM and runs on a 12th Gen Intel Core i9-12900K at 3.20 GHz. It processed the Central Asia maps in about 3
minutes start to finish, and the Russian Federation maps in about 20 minutes. In the script I set splitter to use 4Gb of RAM and mkgmap to use
16Gb. If your box has less RAM you will have to adjust those settings and your scripts will run longer.
